findings.summary: At dusk Hadu and Paltu sit at Muhuria’s thatched-roof verandah with Nisan and Tasa nearby.

Hadu suggests playing; Paltu questions playing with the Nisan alone. They wonder about Maharagu’s late arrival and tease him. Maharagu arrives with his Dhol and challenges the teasing; Hadu replies that they wanted him to hear.

play_preview.short_quote: What can one do with just the Nisan?
play_preview.interpretation: The opening offers camaraderie and an ensemble waiting for another player: a bounded human encounter alongside the existing livelihood discussion. This is our reading of the play, not a documented incident or claim about an identical film scene.
play_preview.possible_addition: In the opening of Bhukha, available in Nirjharini Tripathy’s English translation The Starved, Hadu wants to play music. Paltu asks what one instrument can do alone. Their companion Maharagu arrives carrying his dhol, having overheard their teasing. The banter lets us meet people who know one another, alongside the livelihood the play asks us to consider.
